mainTopic: Placing the קטורת inside, the מעלה עשן requirement, and leaving a holy place or one's רב without turning one's back
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point: the כהן גדול piles the קטורת starting from the far side so he will not burn himself. A ברייתא then teaches from 'לִפְנֵי ה׳' that the קטורת is put on the coals inside קודש הקדשים. This rejects the צדוקים, who wanted it lit outside because of the פסוק 'כִּי בֶּעָנָן אֵרָאֶה'. The חכמים explain that this פסוק requires a מעלה עשן, a smoke-raising herb, and that leaving it or any spice out brings מיתה. The גמרא asks why that is not already a death penalty for an empty entry, and רב ששת and רב אשי each describe a case that explains it. The גמרא then asks why a second פסוק, 'וְכִסָּה', is needed, and gives several answers: root and leaf, יום הכפורים and the whole year, מצוה and לעכב, and עונש and אזהרה. A ברייתא of רבי אליעזר explains that the warning came before נדב ואביהוא died, and that they actually died for ruling on a הלכה in front of משה. Finally, the גמרא learns from שלמה at גבעון that one leaves a holy place without turning one's back, and applies this to כהנים, לוים, ישראל and a תלמיד leaving his רב, with stories about רבי אלעזר and רבא.

steps.title: Why the incense is piled from the far side
steps.stepSummary: This line finishes the earlier explanation: the כהן גדול should not start piling the קטורת on the side closest to him, so he will not burn himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that you do not begin in front of you, lest you be burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a point from the previous section. It gives the reason the כהן גדול spreads the קטורת starting from the far side of the מחתה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose he put the קטורת down near himself first and then spread it toward the far side. His hand would pass over קטורת that was already burning, and he could get hurt. Starting from the far side keeps his hand away from the smoke and fire.

keyTerms.meaning: you will begin
from in front of you (the side nearest you)
you will be burned

phrases.english: so that you do not begin in front of you,
phrases.notes: That is, from the side closest to the כהן.

phrases.english: lest you be burned.
phrases.notes: His hand would pass over incense that is already burning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a discussion earlier about how the קטורת is piled onto the coals.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The קטורת is piled starting from the far side so that the כהן גדול is not burned.

steps.title: The incense must be placed on the fire inside, not prepared outside
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the פסוק that the קטורת goes onto the fire 'לִפְנֵי ה׳', inside קודש הקדשים. It may not be set up outside and carried in already burning. The ברייתא says this teaching is aimed against the צדוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'And he shall put the קטורת on the fire before ה׳.' This means he should not prepare it outside and then bring it in. This comes to exclude the opinion of the צדוקים, who say he should prepare it outside and bring it in.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins with a ברייתא. It teaches where the קטורת is put on the coals, and it names the group it is arguing against: the צדוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'לִפְנֵי ה׳' tell us the placing happens in front of God, which means inside קודש הקדשים. So the כהן גדול carries in coals and קטורת separately, and only puts the קטורת on the fire once he is inside. The צדוקים held the opposite: light it in the היכל first and walk in with smoke already rising.

keyTerms.meaning: the Rabbis taught (introduces a ברייתא)
the incense
prepare it outside and bring it in
to exclude the opinion (literally 'to remove from the heart') of
the Sadducees, a sect that rejected the חכמים' interpretation of the Torah

steps.whyThisMatters: This was a real dispute over how the עבודה of יום הכפורים was done. The ברייתא's wording makes clear that the halacha deliberately rejects the צדוקים' practice.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְנָתַן אֶת הַקְּטוֹרֶת עַל הָאֵשׁ לִפְנֵי ה׳״ —
phrases.english: "And he shall put the incense upon the fire before ה׳" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא טז:יג

phrases.english: that he should not prepare it outside and bring it in.
phrases.notes: Outside means in the היכל.

phrases.english: This is to exclude the view of the Sadducees,
who say he should prepare it outside and bring it in.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: וְנָתַן אֶת הַקְּטוֹרֶת עַל הָאֵשׁ לִפְנֵי ה׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the location where the קטורת is placed on the fire.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קטורת is placed on the coals inside קודש הקדשים, not prepared outside, which rejects the צדוקים' view.

steps.title: What verse did the צדוקים rely on?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what source the צדוקים used for their view.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did they interpret?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the next step: what פסוק did the צדוקים expound?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before rejecting the צדוקים' view, the גמרא wants to know what it was built on. This prepares for the חכמים' answer to their reading.

keyTerms.meaning: what did they expound / what was their source?

phrases.english: What did they expound?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the opposing view mentioned in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק the צדוקים used to say the קטורת is prepared outside.

steps.title: The צדוקים' verse: 'I will appear in a cloud'
steps.stepSummary: The צדוקים relied on 'כִּי בֶּעָנָן אֵרָאֶה עַל הַכַּפּוֹרֶת'. They read it to mean the cloud of קטורת must already exist when the כהן גדול enters.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For in a cloud I will appear upon the Ark cover.' This teaches that he should prepare it outside and bring it in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by giving the צדוקים' פסוק and how they read it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The צדוקים argued that God appears 'in a cloud', so the cloud must already be there when the כהן גדול comes in. That would mean the קטורת has to be lit outside first. This is their reasoning, not the halacha.

keyTerms.meaning: cloud (here, the cloud of incense smoke)
I will appear
the Ark cover
it teaches

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'מְלַמֵּד' here is the צדוקים' reading, not the חכמים' conclusion. The halacha follows the ברייתא in step 2.

phrases.english: "For in a cloud I will appear upon the Ark cover" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא טז:ב

phrases.english: this teaches that he should prepare it outside and bring it in.
phrases.notes: This is how the צדוקים read the verse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The צדוקים used 'כִּי בֶּעָנָן אֵרָאֶה עַל הַכַּפּוֹרֶת' to argue that the cloud must exist before entry.

steps.title: The חכמים point to the explicit verse
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים object to the צדוקים: the Torah already says plainly that the קטורת is put on the fire 'לִפְנֵי ה׳', inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים said to them: But hasn't it already been stated, 'And he shall put the קטורת upon the fire before ה׳'?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים challenge the צדוקים by quoting the פסוק that clearly says the placing happens inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The צדוקים' reading cannot override a פסוק that directly describes the action. 'לִפְנֵי ה׳' sets the place where the קטורת meets the fire, so preparing it outside contradicts the plain text.

keyTerms.meaning: the Sages
but hasn't it already been stated?

phrases.english: The Sages said to them,
but has it not already been stated:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְנָתַן אֶת הַקְּטוֹרֶת עַל הָאֵשׁ לִפְנֵי ה׳״.
phrases.english: "And he shall put the incense upon the fire before ה׳."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם חֲכָמִים, וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the צדוקים' reading given in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The צדוקים' claim that the קטורת is prepared outside.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An explicit פסוק places the putting of the קטורת on the fire 'לִפְנֵי ה׳', inside קודש הקדשים.

steps.title: Then what does 'I will appear in a cloud' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask: if the קטורת is put on inside, what is the purpose of the פסוק 'כִּי בֶּעָנָן אֵרָאֶה'? The answer comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what does the verse come to teach: 'For in a cloud I will appear upon the Ark cover'?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The חכמים now have to explain the צדוקים' פסוק in a different way, and step 7 gives that explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the חכמים reject the צדוקים' reading, the פסוק still needs a meaning, since every פסוק teaches something. 'מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר' opens the חכמים' own interpretation.

keyTerms.meaning: if so
what does the verse come to teach?

phrases.english: If so, what does the verse come to teach:
"For in a cloud I will appear upon the Ark cover" —
phrases.notes: The sentence continues into the next passage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the צדוקים' reading in step 5, the חכמים set up their own explanation of that פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The correct meaning of 'כִּי בֶּעָנָן אֵרָאֶה עַל הַכַּפּוֹרֶת', given that the קטורת is placed inside.

steps.title: The cloud verse teaches that a smoke-raising spice is required
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'כִּי בֶּעָנָן אֵרָאֶה' teaches that the כהן גדול puts מעלה עשן into the קטורת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches that he puts a smoke-raiser into it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 6: what is the point of 'כִּי בֶּעָנָן אֵרָאֶה' if the קטורת is put on the fire inside? The answer is that it teaches an ingredient requirement, not a time requirement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The צדוקים read the 'cloud' as a cloud that already exists when the כהן גדול enters. The חכמים read it as a cloud that must exist in the end. That requires an ingredient, מעלה עשן, which makes the smoke rise like a column. So the פסוק is about how the קטורת is made, not where it is lit.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'smoke-raiser': an herb added to the קטורת that makes the smoke rise straight up
'It teaches': introduces what a פסוק comes to teach
Cloud: here, the cloud of קטורת smoke

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree there is a cloud. The argument is only about when it forms. The צדוקים say it must exist before he walks in. The חכמים say it forms inside, and the פסוק is telling us what ingredient makes that cloud happen.

phrases.english: It teaches that he puts into it a smoke-raiser.
phrases.notes: This is the answer to 'what does כי בענן teach?' from step 6.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question asked in step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'כִּי בֶּעָנָן אֵרָאֶה' teaches that מעלה עשן must be put into the קטורת. It does not teach that the קטורת is lit outside.

steps.title: A second verse as the source for the smoke-raiser
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the requirement of מעלה עשן comes from and cites 'וְכִסָּה עֲנַן הַקְּטוֹרֶת אֶת הַכַּפּוֹרֶת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that he puts a smoke-raiser into it? As it says: 'And the cloud of the incense shall cover the Ark cover.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק that directly commands the cloud to cover the כפורת. This is the source for the מעלה עשן requirement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cloud that rises and 'covers' the כפורת needs an ingredient that makes the smoke climb. So this פסוק is read as a command to include מעלה עשן. Its wording ties the cloud directly to the action of burning the קטורת, and this sets up the punishment stated in the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And from where?': asks for a source
'As it says': introduces a פסוק
The gold cover on top of the ארון

phrases.english: And from where do we know that he puts into it a smoke-raiser?
As it is said: 'And the cloud of the incense shall cover the Ark cover.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא טז:יג. The same פסוק continues 'וְלֹא יָמוּת', which connects to the death penalty in the next step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an explicit פסוק as the source for the requirement introduced in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: The requirement to include מעלה עשן in the קטורת
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא טז:יג: 'וְכִסָּה עֲנַן הַקְּטוֹרֶת אֶת הַכַּפּוֹרֶת'

steps.title: Leaving out the smoke-raiser or any spice makes him liable to death
steps.stepSummary: If the כהן גדול did not include מעלה עשן, or left out any one of the spices, he is חייב מיתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: So if he did not put in a smoke-raiser, or if he left out one of all its spices, he is liable to death.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes with the practical result. Incomplete קטורת brings a death penalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule now covers more than מעלה עשן. Missing any of the spices counts as burning incomplete קטורת, and that brings מיתה בידי שמים. This ruling is what the גמרא is about to question.

keyTerms.meaning: The spices or ingredients of the קטורת
He left out (an ingredient)
Liable to death (here, at the hands of Heaven)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's final reading: the קטורת is lit inside, 'לִפְנֵי ה׳'. 'כִּי בֶּעָנָן' teaches that מעלה עשן is required. Incomplete קטורת brings a death penalty.

phrases.aramaic: הָא לֹא נָתַן בָּהּ מַעֲלֵה עָשָׁן,
phrases.english: Thus, if he did not put into it a smoke-raiser,
or if he left out one of all its spices,
he is liable to death.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לֹא נָתַן בָּהּ מַעֲלֵה עָשָׁן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the punishment that follows from the requirement derived in steps 7–8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Burning קטורת without מעלה עשן, or without any one of its spices, makes the כהן גדול חייב מיתה.

steps.title: Why not make him liable for entering for no purpose?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ruling. He should already be liable for an empty entry (ביאה ריקנית) into קודש הקדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him get it from the fact that he is making an empty entry!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's reason for the death penalty. It says there is an earlier, simpler reason he deserves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Entering קודש הקדשים without a proper עבודה is itself punishable by death. If his קטורת is invalid, his entry was empty, so the death penalty should already apply when he walks in. Why does the ברייתא tie it to the burning?

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let him derive it from…': suggests a simpler, earlier source for the same result
An 'empty entry': entering קודש הקדשים without a valid עבודה
He enters / brings in

phrases.english: But let him derive it (the liability)
from the fact that he is making an empty entry!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִיפּוֹק לֵיהּ דְּקָא מְעַיֵּיל בִּיאָה רֵיקָנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason for the death penalty given in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that he is חייב מיתה for burning incomplete קטורת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His entry was already empty because the קטורת is invalid, so the death penalty should come from the entry. Making the burning the cause seems unnecessary.

steps.title: רב ששת: the entry was accidental, the burning was deliberate
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that the case is where he entered בשוגג but burned the incomplete קטורת במזיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: Here we are dealing with a case where he acted unknowingly about the entry, and deliberately about the burning.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת describes a specific case in which the entry cannot bring a death penalty but the burning can.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A death penalty בידי שמים only applies to a deliberate act (מזיד). If the entry was a mistake, it brings no death penalty. The only deliberate act left is burning the incomplete קטורת, so the ברייתא has to name the burning as the cause.

keyTerms.meaning: 'With what are we dealing here?': limits a teaching to a specific case
Acting by mistake or without knowing
Acting deliberately, knowing it is forbidden
The act of burning the קטורת

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
Here, with what are we dealing?
For example, where he acted unknowingly regarding the entry,
and acted deliberately regarding the burning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case limitation (אוקימתא): the entry and the burning differ in intent
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every case of incomplete קטורת also includes a punishable empty entry, so naming the burning seems unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the entry was שוגג and the burning was מזיד, only the burning brings a death penalty.

steps.title: רב אשי: he brought in one complete and one incomplete set
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that even if both acts were deliberate, the case is where he brought in two sets of קטורת. The complete set makes the entry valid, and the incomplete set brings liability for the burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: You can even say he was deliberate about both. The case is where he brought in two burnings, one complete and one missing. For the entry he is not liable, since he brought in a complete one. For the burning he is liable, since he is burning incomplete קטורת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different answer to the same קשיא. It works even when he acted deliberately in every way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because he brought in a complete set of קטורת, his entry had a valid purpose and was not 'empty'. He still also burned an incomplete set, and that act alone brings the death penalty. So the burning is the only source of liability, with no need to assume a mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You can even say': the answer works even in the harder case
Complete (קטורת with all its spices)
Incomplete (missing a spice)
He is liable

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to explain why the ברייתא blames the burning and not the entry. רב ששת: the entry was a mistake and the burning was deliberate. רב אשי: he also brought in a complete set, so the entry was valid.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
You can even say he acted deliberately in this and in that,
and the case is where he brought in two sets of incense to burn,
one complete and one incomplete.
For the entry he is not liable,
since he brought in a complete one;
for the burning he is liable,
since he is burning incomplete incense.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא הֵזִיד בְּזוֹ וּבָזוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative answer to the קשיא of step 10, different from רב ששת's answer in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative case limitation: two sets of קטורת make the entry valid
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If he acted deliberately in both, the empty entry should bring the death penalty.
steps.terutzMaskana: Bringing in a complete set makes the entry valid, so liability comes only from burning the incomplete set.

steps.title: Why bring a second verse for the smoke-raiser?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's line that 'וכסה' teaches מעלה עשן. It then asks why a second פסוק is needed when the first one already taught it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'And from where do we know that he puts a smoke-raiser into it? The verse says: וכסה.' But this is one verse added onto another verse!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the earlier ברייתא and challenges it. The ברייתא seems to prove the same thing twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא already learned מעלה עשן from 'כי בענן אראה על הכפרת'. It then asked 'from where?' again and answered with 'וכסה'. The question is that a second פסוק should not be needed to teach the exact same law.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said.' This is how the גמרא quotes a ברייתא it is about to discuss.
A smoke-raising herb added to the קטורת so the smoke rises straight up
'The verse teaches.' It introduces a פסוק as the source.
'A verse for a verse?' This means: why is a second פסוק needed for something already taught?

steps.confusionAlert: The 'first verse' here is 'כי בענן אראה על הכפרת' from earlier in the ברייתא. 'וכסה' is the second verse. The question is about why the second one is needed.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר: וּמִנַּיִין שֶׁנּוֹתֵן בָּהּ מַעֲלֵה עָשָׁן,
phrases.english: The Master said: And from where do we know that he puts a smoke-raiser into it,
phrases.notes: Quoting the ברייתא

phrases.english: The verse says: 'And it shall cover.'
A verse for another verse?
phrases.notes: The first verse already taught this law

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא's derivation from step 8 and questions why it uses two פסוקים
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of 'וכסה' as a source for מעלה עשן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מעלה עשן was already derived from 'כי בענן אראה', so a second derivation looks unnecessary

steps.title: רב יוסף: the first verse teaches the leaf, the second adds the root
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that each פסוק teaches something different. The first teaches the leaf of the smoke-raiser, and 'וכסה' adds its root.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: This is what the ברייתא means. From the first verse I only know about the leaf of the smoke-raiser. From where do I know about the root of the smoke-raiser? The verse says: 'וכסה'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question by giving each פסוק its own job. The second פסוק is not repeating the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plant has two parts, the leaf and the root. According to רב יוסף, the basic פסוק requires the leaf, and 'וכסה' adds a requirement to also put in the root. Since each פסוק teaches something new, there is no extra פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what it means.' It introduces a re-reading of an earlier text.
'I only know.' This is what the first source covers on its own.
Leaf of the plant
Root of the plant

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: This is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא עֲלֵה מַעֲלֵה עָשָׁן,
phrases.english: I have only the leaf of the smoke-raiser,
phrases.notes: Learned from the first verse

phrases.english: From where do I know the root of the smoke-raiser?
The verse says: 'And it shall cover.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'verse for a verse' question
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two פסוקים into two separate teachings
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both פסוקים seemed to teach the same thing
steps.terutzMaskana: The first פסוק teaches the leaf, and 'וכסה' adds the root

steps.title: אביי: another ברייתא shows the root is the main smoke-maker
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף with a ברייתא saying that the root makes the smoke rise like a column and fill the whole House. This means the root is the main ingredient, not an extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But the opposite was taught! A ברייתא teaches: He put in the root of the smoke-raiser, and the smoke rose straight up like a stick until it reached the ceiling. Once it reached the ceiling, it slowly crept down the walls until the House was filled with smoke, as it says: 'And the House was filled with smoke.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's answer using a different ברייתא. That ברייתא shows the root is the main source of the smoke.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף treated the leaf as the basic requirement and the root as an add-on. The ברייתא shows the root is what actually makes the strong column of smoke. So the root should be the basic requirement from the first פסוק, not something added later.

keyTerms.meaning: The opposite
'It was taught in a ברייתא.' It introduces a ברייתא.
Rising straight up like a column (like a palm tree)
Like a stick or staff
The ceiling (literally 'the sky of the beam')
Walls

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But the opposite was taught!

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: נָתַן בָּהּ עִיקַּר מַעֲלֵה עָשָׁן,
phrases.english: As it was taught: He put the root of the smoke-raiser into it,
it would rise up in a column like a stick
until it reached the ceiling.
Once it reached the ceiling,
it would slowly creep down along the walls
until the House was filled with smoke,
as it says: 'And the House was filled with smoke'!
phrases.notes: ישעיה ו:ד

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's answer from step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that the leaf is basic and the root is an add-on
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows the root makes the main smoke column, so the root must be the basic requirement

steps.title: אביי: the first verse teaches the root, the second adds the leaf
steps.stepSummary: אביי reverses רב יוסף's reading. The first פסוק requires the root, and 'וכסה' adds that the leaf must also be included.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: This is what the ברייתא means. From the first verse I only know about the root of the smoke-raiser. From where do I know about the leaf of the smoke-raiser? The verse says: 'וכסה'.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a new answer to the 'verse for a verse' question. It fits with the ברייתא he just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי keeps רב יוסף's idea that each פסוק teaches a different part of the plant, but he swaps the parts. The root is the main smoke-maker, so it comes from the basic פסוק. 'וכסה' adds that even the leaf must be put in.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather.' This marks that the earlier answer is dropped and a new one is given.

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, both parts of the smoke-raising plant are required in the קטורת. The first פסוק teaches the root, which is the main smoke-producer, and 'וכסה' adds the leaf. So the ברייתא's two פסוקים are not repeating each other. The גמרא goes on to give other answers to the same question in the next steps.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said: This is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא עִיקַּר מַעֲלֵה עָשָׁן,
phrases.english: I have only the root of the smoke-raiser,
phrases.notes: Learned from the first verse

phrases.english: From where do I know the leaf of the smoke-raiser?
The verse says: 'And it shall cover.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב יוסף's answer, which was refuted in step 15, with a reversed version
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reversing which plant part each פסוק teaches
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יוסף held that the leaf is basic and the root is added
steps.terutzMaskana: The root is basic from the first פסוק, and 'וכסה' adds the leaf

steps.title: רב ששת: the second verse extends the rule to שילה and the בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that the first פסוק only teaches the מעלה עשן for the אהל מועד in the desert. ״וְכִסָּה״ extends it to שילה and the בית עולמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: From the first verse I only know this rule for the אהל מועד in the desert. How do I know it applies to שילה and the בית עולמים? The verse says: "וְכִסָּה."
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives a new answer to the question from Step 13. He says the second פסוק is not extra, because it teaches that the rule applies in later places too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was why the Torah repeats the מעלה עשן rule. רב ששת says the first פסוק is limited to the משכן in the desert. ״וְכִסָּה״ teaches that the same rule applies in שילה and in the בית המקדש in ירושלים.

keyTerms.meaning: The Tent of Meeting (משכן) in the desert
The place where the משכן stood for many years in ארץ ישראל
The eternal House, meaning the בית המקדש in ירושלים
"I only have": the verse by itself only teaches this much
"The verse teaches": introduces the פסוק that adds the extra case

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד שֶׁבַּמִּדְבָּר.
phrases.english: I only know this for the Tent of Meeting in the wilderness.
phrases.notes: This is what the first verse alone would teach.

phrases.english: From where do we know it for Shiloh and the eternal Temple?
The verse states: "And it shall cover."
phrases.notes: ״וְכִסָּה״ extends the rule to every place where the קטורת is offered.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד שֶׁבַּמִּדְבָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from the one given by רב יוסף and אביי to the question in Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each verse covers a different place: one covers the desert, the other covers later locations.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second פסוק seems to repeat the first one for no reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״וְכִסָּה״ extends the מעלה עשן requirement to שילה and the בית המקדש.

steps.title: Challenge: another verse already teaches that the rule applies in later places
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the rule for later places already comes from ״וכן יעשה לאהל מועד השוכן אתם״, so ״וְכִסָּה״ is not needed for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this is already learned from the verse: "And so shall he do for the אהל מועד that dwells with them"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב ששת's answer. It says a different פסוק already teaches that the יום הכפורים service applies wherever the שכינה dwells.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "that dwells with them" teaches that the service is the same in every place where the שכינה rests: the desert, שילה, and the בית המקדש. So ״וְכִסָּה״ cannot be needed for that. This reopens the original question, and step 19 answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: "And so shall he do for the Tent of Meeting" (ויקרא ט״ז:ט״ז)
"That dwells with them": wherever the שכינה rests among ישראל
"It comes out": it is already derived from there

phrases.english: This is learned from "And so shall he do for the Tent of Meeting
that dwells with them"!
phrases.notes: The rule for later places is already taught by this verse, so ״וְכִסָּה״ is not needed for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי, מִ״וְּכֵן יַעֲשֶׂה לְאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד הַשּׁוֹכֵן אִתָּם״ נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רב ששת's reading in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's claim that ״וְכִסָּה״ extends the rule to שילה and the בית המקדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A different פסוק already teaches that the rule applies in every place. So ״וְכִסָּה״ would be extra again.

steps.title: Revised reading: the second verse extends the rule to the whole year
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords רב ששת's answer. The first פסוק teaches the מעלה עשן for יום הכפורים, and ״וְכִסָּה״ extends it to the daily קטורת all year.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what he meant: From the first verse I only know it for יום הכפורים. How do I know it for the rest of the days of the year? The verse says: "And it shall cover."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes רב ששת's answer. The extension is now about time, not place: from יום הכפורים to every other day of the year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer failed because another פסוק already covers other places. So the גמרא changes what ״וְכִסָּה״ adds. Now it teaches that the daily קטורת in the היכל also needs a מעלה עשן, not only the יום הכפורים קטורת in the קודש הקדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: "Rather, this is what he said": the גמרא rewords an earlier statement
The Day of Atonement, when the כהן גדול brings קטורת into the קודש הקדשים
The rest of the days of the year, when the daily קטורת is burned in the היכל

steps.confusionAlert: This is still רב ששת's answer, just reworded. The גמרא is not dropping him. It changes the extension from places (desert to מקדש) to times (יום הכפורים to the whole year).

phrases.english: Rather, this is what he said:
I only know this for Yom Kippur.
From where do we know it for the rest of the days of the year?
The verse states: "And it shall cover."
phrases.notes: ״וְכִסָּה״ requires the מעלה עשן in every קטורת of the year.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָכִי קָאָמַר: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 18 by rewording רב ששת's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewording (אלא הכי קאמר): the extension is moved from place to time.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״וְכִסָּה״ extends the rule to other places, which another פסוק already teaches.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״וְכִסָּה״ extends the מעלה עשן requirement from יום הכפורים to the daily קטורת all year.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the מעלה עשן is part of every קטורת, not only the special יום הכפורים offering.

steps.title: רב אשי: one verse gives the מצוה, the other makes it indispensable
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says both פסוקים deal with the same קטורת. One teaches the מצוה, and the other teaches that leaving out the מעלה עשן makes the service invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: One verse teaches the מצוה, and one verse teaches that it is indispensable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a new answer to the question of why two פסוקים are needed. He says the second פסוק upgrades the rule from "you should" to "without it, it does not count."
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain מצוה tells you what to do, but if you skip it the act may still be valid. The second פסוק teaches לעכב: without the מעלה עשן, the קטורת is invalid. So the two פסוקים teach two different levels of the same rule.

keyTerms.meaning: One verse for the מצוה: it is the proper way to do it
And one verse to make it indispensable: without it, the service is invalid

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
One is for the מצוה, and one is to make it indispensable.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: חַד לְמִצְוָה, וְחַד לְעַכֵּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another answer to Step 13's question, different from רב יוסף, אביי, and רב ששת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different legal strength: one פסוק gives the basic מצוה, the other makes it לעכב.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים seem to teach the same thing twice.
steps.terutzMaskana: Without the מעלה עשן, the קטורת is invalid.

steps.title: רבא: one verse gives the punishment, the other gives the warning
steps.stepSummary: רבא says one פסוק teaches the punishment (מיתה) for leaving out the מעלה עשן, and the other gives the אזהרה (the warning not to do it).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: One verse is for the punishment, and one verse is for the warning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives one more answer to why two פסוקים are needed. One teaches the עונש and the other teaches the אזהרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah does not punish without first warning (אין עונשין אלא אם כן מזהירין). So the Torah needs one פסוק for the punishment of death and a separate פסוק for the warning. This is why both פסוקים are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: One verse for the punishment (here, מיתה)
And one verse for the warning, the actual prohibition

steps.whatToRemember: Step 13 asked why ״וְכִסָּה״ is needed. Here are the answers: רב יוסף and אביי say one פסוק teaches the root and the other the leaf. רב ששת (reworded) says one teaches יום הכפורים and the other the whole year. רב אשי says one teaches the מצוה and the other makes it לעכב. רבא says one teaches the עונש and the other the אזהרה.

phrases.english: Rava said:
One is for the punishment, and one is for the warning.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: חַד לְעוֹנֶשׁ, וְחַד לְאַזְהָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further answer alongside רב אשי's, again explaining why the second פסוק is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Division into עונש and אזהרה, since the Torah needs both before it punishes.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second פסוק seems to be extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: One פסוק gives the death penalty for leaving out the מעלה עשן, and the other gives the prohibition itself.
steps.whyThisMatters: This uses the general rule that the Torah punishes only after it warns, so a punishment needs its own separate source for the warning.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבא: one phrase is the punishment, the other is the warning
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר teaches that ״ולא ימות״ is the עונש and ״כי בענן אראה״ is the אזהרה. This matches רבא's answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר says, "that he not die" is the punishment, and "for in a cloud I will appear" is the warning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that says exactly what רבא just said. One part of the פסוק gives the punishment, and the other gives the warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 21, רבא split the two sources into an עונש and an אזהרה. Here רבי אליעזר does the same with two phrases in ויקרא ט״ז:ב. ״ולא ימות״ (death) is the punishment. ״כי בענן אראה״ (the cloud of smoke must appear) is the warning not to leave out the מעלה עשן.

keyTerms.meaning: Punishment, here מִיתָה (death)
A warning or prohibition: the Torah's command not to do something
It was taught in a ברייתא
Cloud, here the cloud of קטורת smoke

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
"That he not die" is the punishment,
phrases.notes: ויקרא ט״ז:ב

phrases.english: "For in a cloud I will appear" is the warning.
phrases.notes: The cloud must appear, so the smoke-raiser may not be left out

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא supporting רבא's split into עונש and אזהרה
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that one source is the עונש and the other is the אזהרה
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי אליעזר on ויקרא ט״ז:ב

steps.title: The warning was given before the sons' death, and the punishment after
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. It proves from the פסוקים that the אזהרה came before מיתת בני אהרן and the עונש came after.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think both were said before the death of בני אהרן, so the verse says "after the death of the two sons of אהרן." One might think both were said after their death, so the verse says "for in a cloud I will appear on the כפורת." How so? The אזהרה was before the death, and the עונש was after the death.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now asks when each of the two rules was given. It concludes that the warning came before נדב ואביהוא died, and the punishment came after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״אחרי מות שני בני אהרן״ shows that this פרשה was said after the deaths, so not everything came before. ״כי בענן אראה״ is in the future tense, so it shows that at least part of it was said earlier. The answer that fits both: the אזהרה came first and the עונש came later.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought (opens a wrong guess that the ברייתא will reject)
Therefore the verse says (brings the פסוק that rejects the wrong guess)
How so? (introduces the answer that fits both sources)
The cover on top of the ארון

steps.confusionAlert: "Before the death" does not mean the punishment was hidden. It means only the warning had been said so far. The punishment of death was stated only after נדב ואביהוא died.

phrases.english: One might think both were said
before the death of Aaron's sons;

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אַחֲרֵי מוֹת שְׁנֵי בְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן״.
phrases.english: therefore the verse says: "After the death of the two sons of Aaron."
phrases.notes: ויקרא ט״ז:א

phrases.english: One might think both were said
after the death of the two sons of Aaron;

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״כִּי בֶּעָנָן אֵרָאֶה עַל הַכַּפּוֹרֶת״.
phrases.english: therefore the verse says: "For in a cloud I will appear upon the Ark cover."
How so?
The warning was before the death,
and the punishment was after the death.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל יִהְיוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם אֲמוּרִין קוֹדֶם מִיתַת בְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and adds when each rule was given
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אזהרה for the מעלה עשן was given before מיתת בני אהרן. The עונש was given after.

steps.title: How does the verse show the warning came earlier?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how ״כי בענן אראה״ proves that the warning was said before the deaths.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the derivation?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the proof. How do we know from ״כי בענן אראה״ that this part was said before the sons died? This question sets up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״אחרי מות״ clearly shows that the פרשה came after the deaths. But nothing in ״כי בענן אראה״ obviously points to an earlier time. So the גמרא asks what in that phrase shows it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the derivation? (how is this learned from the פסוק)

phrases.english: What is the derivation?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the proof behind the ברייתא's second derivation
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How ״כי בענן אראה״ shows that the warning came before the deaths

steps.title: רבא: 'I will appear' is future tense, so the cloud had not yet appeared
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that ״אראה״ means 'I will appear.' That shows it was said before the משכן was set up, which was also before the sons died.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the verse says "For in a cloud I will appear", and it had not yet appeared.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers from the grammar of the word. ״אראה״ is future tense, so the cloud had not yet appeared when this was said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the cloud had not appeared yet, the משכן was not yet up and running. נדב ואביהוא died on the day the משכן was set up, so this warning must have been given before their death.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse says
And it had not yet appeared

phrases.english: Rava said: the verse says:
"For in a cloud I will appear"
and it had not yet appeared.
phrases.notes: Future tense, so this was said before the משכן was set up

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The future tense ״אראה״ shows the cloud had not yet appeared, so the warning was given before the deaths

steps.title: If no punishment had been given yet, why were בני אהרן punished?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects. Only the warning existed at the time, so why did נדב ואביהוא die?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what is the reason they were punished?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with the ברייתא's timeline. If the death penalty was announced only after the sons died, how could they be killed for this?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah does not punish someone with death before that punishment has been stated. The ברייתא said the עונש came only after their death. So their death must have had a different cause.

keyTerms.meaning: But then, what is the reason?
They were punished

phrases.english: But then, what is the reason they were punished?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the result of the timeline proven in steps 23 and 25
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the עונש was stated only after מיתת בני אהרן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There can be no death penalty before the punishment was stated, yet בני אהרן did die

steps.title: They died for ruling on a הלכה in front of משה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי אליעזר says that בני אהרן died because they ruled on a הלכה in front of משה רבן, not because of the קטורת.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי אליעזר says, בני אהרן died only because they ruled on a הלכה in front of משה, their teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that their death had a different cause. They decided a הלכה on their own while their teacher משה was right there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This removes the problem. They were not punished for the missing מעלה עשן, which had no punishment yet. Their sin was disrespect for their teacher, which is a separate offense.

keyTerms.meaning: They gave a ruling of הלכה
In front of משה, their teacher
As it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the well-known rule that a student may not rule on a הלכה in front of his teacher.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
Aaron's sons died only
because they ruled on a הלכה
in front of Moses their teacher.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: לֹא מֵתוּ בְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 26 by giving a different reason for their death
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different cause for the punishment
steps.terutzHavaAmina: They died for the missing מעלה עשן
steps.terutzMaskana: They died for ruling on a הלכה in front of משה

steps.title: What did they learn from the verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which דרשה led בני אהרן to bring their own fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did they interpret?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what ruling בני אהרן actually made. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying they 'ruled on a הלכה' is still vague. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק they learned from, and what they concluded from it.

keyTerms.meaning: What did they interpret (from the פסוק)?

phrases.english: What did they interpret?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the details of the ruling mentioned in step 27
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The דרשה that בני אהרן ruled on

steps.title: Fire comes from heaven, but there is a מצוה to bring regular fire too
steps.stepSummary: They learned from ״ונתנו בני אהרן הכהן אש על המזבח״ that even though fire comes down from heaven, there is a מצוה to bring man-made fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And the sons of Aaron the כהן shall put fire on the altar": even though fire comes down from heaven, it is a מצוה to bring ordinary fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the דרשה they made. They concluded that people must bring their own fire, even though heavenly fire was coming.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their ruling was actually correct as הלכה. Their sin was not a wrong conclusion. It was deciding the matter themselves instead of asking משה.

keyTerms.meaning: Fire coming down from heaven
Ordinary, man-made (here, ordinary fire)
The altar

steps.whatToRemember: The warning about the מעלה עשן was given before נדב ואביהוא died, and the punishment came after. They died for ruling on a הלכה in front of משה. Their ruling, that one must bring man-made fire, was correct, but they should not have decided it on their own.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume their ruling was wrong. The דרשה is accepted הלכה. The sin was ruling in front of their teacher.

phrases.english: "And the sons of Aaron the priest shall put
phrases.notes: ויקרא א׳:ז

phrases.english: fire upon the altar"

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהָאֵשׁ יוֹרֶדֶת מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם,
phrases.english: even though the fire comes down from heaven,
it is a מצוה to bring ordinary fire.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנָתְנוּ בְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֵן אֵשׁ עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 28 with the actual דרשה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From ״ונתנו״ they learned that even with heavenly fire, there is a מצוה to bring man-made fire

steps.title: Where do we learn that the כהן גדול walks out backward?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that the כהן גדול exits the way he entered and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: he goes out the same way he came in. Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new topic. It quotes a line from the משנה and asks for its source in the פסוקים, which sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "The way he came in" means he does not turn his back on the ארון. He walks out backward, still facing it. The גמרא wants to know which verse teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: the way he entered (facing forward toward the holy place)
from where do we know these things? (a request for a source)
he went out

steps.confusionAlert: "The way he came in" is not about which door or path he takes. It is about which direction his face points. He keeps facing the holy place even while leaving.

phrases.english: He went out and came away
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה about the כהן גדול leaving the קודש הקדשים.

phrases.english: the way he entered.
phrases.notes: Facing the ארון and walking backward.

phrases.english: From where are these words derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the נדב ואביהוא discussion and opens a new topic based on the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A verse that teaches you must leave a holy place without turning your back on it.

steps.title: The source is the verse about שלמה at גבעון
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני, quoting רבי יונתן, cites the verse "ויבא שלמה לבמה אשר בגבעון ירושלים".
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: the verse says, "And שלמה came to the במה that was in גבעון, ירושלים."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the verse that will be the source. The verse alone does not explain anything yet. It is setting up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse is strange because it names two different places, גבעון and ירושלים, as if they were one. The answer will be built on that oddness.

keyTerms.meaning: the verse says
a raised altar or place of offering; here, the great במה at גבעון
the city where the משכן's main במה stood in שלמה's time

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said,
Rabbi Yonatan said,
the verse states:
"And Solomon came to the high place
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב א:יג

phrases.english: that was at Gibeon, Jerusalem",

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question by bringing a verse.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse "ויבא שלמה לבמה אשר בגבעון ירושלים".

steps.title: Why does the verse put גבעון and ירושלים together?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן points out that the verse is odd: what does גבעון have to do with ירושלים?
steps.simpleTranslation: But what does גבעון have to do with ירושלים? They are two separate places.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן points to a problem in the wording of the verse. This prepares the way for the דרשה that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person goes to גבעון or to ירושלים. The verse cannot mean he went to both at once. Since the wording looks wrong, it must be there to teach us something.

keyTerms.meaning: but what does this have to do with...? (a question that points out an odd connection)
next to, in relation to

phrases.english: Now what does Gibeon have to do
with Jerusalem?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מָה עִנְיַן גִּבְעוֹן אֵצֶל יְרוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out the oddness in the verse just quoted, which drives the דרשה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the verse join two different places, גבעון and ירושלים?

steps.title: Leaving is compared to arriving, so he faced the במה both ways
steps.stepSummary: The verse compares שלמה's leaving גבעון to his arriving there. Just as he faced the במה when he came, he still faced it when he left.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the verse compares his leaving גבעון for ירושלים to his coming from ירושלים to גבעון. When he came, his face was toward the במה, the normal way people arrive. So too when he left, his face was still toward the במה, the same way as when he arrived.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן solves the odd wording. The verse links the trip in with the trip out, so both were done facing the holy place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When you walk toward a place, you naturally face it. The verse ties the leaving to the arriving, which teaches that you must keep facing the holy place even as you leave. In other words, you walk backward. This is the source for the כהן גדול leaving "דרך כניסתו".

keyTerms.meaning: compares, links two things so the rule of one applies to the other (a הֶקֵּשׁ)
his leaving
his arriving
toward, facing

steps.whatToRemember: Source: "בגבעון ירושלים" links leaving to arriving. Just as you face a holy place when you come in, you keep facing it when you leave.

phrases.english: Rather: it compares his exit
from Gibeon to Jerusalem
to his arrival from Jerusalem to Gibeon:
just as on his arrival from Jerusalem to Gibeon
his face was toward the high place,
in the normal manner of arriving,
so too on his exit from Gibeon to Jerusalem
his face was toward the high place,
the same way as his arrival.
phrases.notes: He walked out backward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the odd wording by reading it as a הקש between leaving and arriving.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse links his exit to his entry, so he faced the במה even while leaving. This teaches that one walks out backward from a holy place.

steps.title: כהנים, לוים and ישראל also turn sideways when they leave
steps.stepSummary: The same respect applies to כהנים at their עבודה, לוים on the דוכן and ישראל at the מעמד. When they leave, they turn their faces sideways and do not turn their backs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Likewise, the כהנים at their service, the לוים on their platform and the ישראלים at their watch: when they left, they did not turn around and walk away. They turned their faces sideways and walked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא widens the rule. Others who serve in the מקדש also may not turn their backs on it when they leave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For them the rule is a bit lighter than for the כהן גדול. They do not walk fully backward. They turn to the side so that their back is not facing the holy place. The idea behind both is the same: never show your back to the קדושה.

keyTerms.meaning: the platform where the לוים sang in the מקדש
the group of ישראלים who stood by while the קרבן תמיד was offered
take leave, depart
turn sideways

phrases.english: And likewise, priests at their service,
and Levites on their platform,
and Israelites at their watch,
when they depart,
they would not turn their faces around and walk,
but would turn their faces sideways and walk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the principle from the כהן גדול to everyone serving in the מקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כהנים, לוים and ישראל leaving their posts in the מקדש turn sideways and do not turn their backs.

steps.title: A student leaving his teacher also turns sideways
steps.stepSummary: A תלמיד leaving his רב should not turn his back. He should turn sideways as he walks away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Likewise, a student leaving his teacher should not turn around and walk away. He should turn his face sideways and walk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the same respect to a person: a student leaving his רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The honor owed to a רב is treated like the honor owed to a holy place. So the same sideways leaving applies, even outside the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: student
his teacher
turns sideways

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical rule of כבוד רבו that applies today, even without a מקדש.

phrases.english: And likewise, a student taking leave of his teacher
should not turn his face around and walk,
but should turn his face sideways and walk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the rule further, from the מקדש to a תלמיד and his רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד leaving his רב turns sideways and does not turn his back.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר stayed bowing until רבי יוחנן was out of sight
steps.stepSummary: A story shows the practice. When רבי יוחנן left, רבי אלעזר stayed bowed in his place until his teacher disappeared from view.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what רבי אלעזר did when parting from רבי יוחנן. When רבי יוחנן wanted to leave, רבי אלעזר would bow and stay standing in his place until רבי יוחנן was out of sight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a real example of a student showing this kind of respect to his teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר did even more than turn sideways. He did not move at all until his רב was gone, so his back was never turned toward רבי יוחנן. This brings the rule to life.

keyTerms.meaning: like this case of (introduces an example)
to walk off, to leave
bowing, bending down
was hidden, out of sight

steps.whatToRemember: Never turn your back on קדושה. The כהן גדול walks out backward. כהנים, לוים, ישראל and a תלמיד leaving his רב turn sideways. רבי אלעזר even stayed in place until רבי יוחנן was gone.

phrases.english: As in that case of Rabbi Elazar:

phrases.aramaic: כַּד הֲוָה מִיפְּטַר מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: when he would take leave of Rabbi Yoḥanan,

phrases.aramaic: כַּד הֲוָה בָּעֵי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְסַגּוֹיֵי,
phrases.english: when Rabbi Yoḥanan wanted to walk away,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה גָּחֵין קָאֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אַדּוּכְתֵּיהּ
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar would bow and stand in his place

phrases.aramaic: עַד דַּהֲוָה מִיכַּסֵּי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִינֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: until Rabbi Yoḥanan was hidden from his sight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life example of the תלמיד rule just stated.
steps.raayaObject: The practice of not turning your back on your רב when parting.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The behavior of רבי אלעזר toward his teacher רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר walks backward when leaving רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: When רבי אלעזר wanted to leave רבי יוחנן, he walked backward until רבי יוחנן could no longer see him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when רבי אלעזר wanted to go away, he would walk backward until he was hidden from רבי יוחנן's sight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the story about רבי אלעזר. Before, רבי יוחנן was the one leaving. Now it describes what רבי אלעזר did when he was the one leaving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 36 showed respect when the רב leaves: the student stays bowed. This step shows the other side, when the student leaves: he walks backward so he never shows his back to his רב. Together they show the rule from Step 35 in real life from both directions.

keyTerms.meaning: to walk away, to go off
walks backward
until he is hidden or out of sight

phrases.aramaic: וְכַד הֲוָה בָּעֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לְסַגּוֹיֵי,
phrases.english: And when Rabbi Elazar wanted to walk away,
he would walk backward
phrases.notes: So he would not turn his back to his teacher.

phrases.english: until he was hidden from Rabbi Yochanan's sight.
phrases.notes: Only once out of sight did he walk normally.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכַד הֲוָה בָּעֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לְסַגּוֹיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the רבי אלעזר story from Step 36. Step 36 covered the teacher leaving, and this step covers the student leaving.
steps.raayaObject: The rule from Step 35 that a תלמיד leaving his רב must not turn his back to him.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of רבי אלעזר, who walked backward when leaving רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: רבא walks backward from רב יוסף until he is injured
steps.stepSummary: רבא walked backward when leaving רב יוסף, so carefully that his legs got bruised and the doorway of רב יוסף's house was bloodied.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבא took leave of רב יוסף, he would walk backward until his legs were bruised and the doorstep of רב יוסף's house became stained with blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second story showing the same practice. This time it is רבא leaving his teacher רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story adds how far the respect went. רבא would not turn around even to watch where he was stepping, so he banged his legs and bled. It shows that this כבוד הרב mattered more to him than his own comfort.

keyTerms.meaning: taking leave, saying goodbye
that his legs were bruised or struck
threshold, doorstep
blood

steps.whatToRemember: A תלמיד does not turn his back when leaving his רב. רבי אלעזר and רבא walked backward until they were out of sight, and רבא did so even when it hurt him.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא did not hurt himself on purpose. He got hurt because he refused to turn around and look where he was walking.

phrases.english: Rava, when he would take leave
of Rav Yosef,
would walk backward
until his legs were bruised
phrases.notes: He did not turn to see the obstacles in his way.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִתַּוְּוסָן אִסְקוּפָּתָא דְּבֵי רַב יוֹסֵף דְּמָא.
phrases.english: and the threshold of Rav Yosef's house was stained with blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא כַּד הֲוָה מִיפְּטַר מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story showing the same practice as Step 37. It is more extreme, because רבא kept walking backward even when it caused him injury.
steps.raayaObject: The rule from Step 35 that a student must not turn his back when leaving his רב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of רבא, who walked backward when leaving רב יוסף even when he got hurt.
